reviews.comment: I took his ANTH 317 and 436 classes. He is a very kind professor and passionate about his classes. All the information you need for the tests are in his lectures and slides; though attendance isn't mandatory, I wouldn't recommend skipping. I enjoyed his lectures and would love to take another class with him if I could.

Cannot say enough good things about this class and the prof! Such a kind and caring man. I love Dr. Wachsmann. You can tell he's VERY passionate about Egypt and would tell us some of his excavation experiences. I wish this class was longer so I could have learned more. Gives you the lecture slides/notes, 3 tests & a paper were the only grades.

I took his Ancient Egypt class and it was wonderful. He talks about his own excavations and experience in the field. I love his lectures and he is really nice. I almost got a B in the class and I asked if I can do anything to get an A and he was willing to provide an alternative test choice (harder, but I got an A).

I LOVE Dr. Wachsmann. He is such a sweet man with so much archaeological experience. I've taken 2 of his classes - they were both challenging, but listening to him talk about what he loves is fascinating and worth it. He is incredibly knowledgeable and kind. Visit him during office hours! Ask him about his cats! He's super cool and helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Could barely hear this man talk and I sat in the front row. Biblical archaeology sounded interesting at first but the content is beyond boring. You need to remember dates and random/irrelevant information. Study guides will have 200+ terms but you are only tested on like 30 of them (waste of time). Only grades are 2 tests, an assignment and final.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy
